expectations.text: detection.kql projects Timestamp, ReportId and DeviceId in its final output (XDR required columns), recovered via arg_max/arg_min after any summarize
expectations.evidence: Line 82 `summarize arg_min(Timestamp, *), ... by ProcessKey` recovers the earliest row's columns under their original names; line 93 `project Timestamp, ReportId, DeviceId, DeviceName, ...`. Note the grain is one row per ProcessKey fleet-wide, so DeviceId is that of the earliest device only (documented, rule.md line 28-31).

expectations.text: detection.kql computes the 'seen before' baseline from a window that ends before the recent window starts (a guard gap such as between(ago(30d)..ago(1d)) vs > ago(1d)), not an overlapping window
expectations.evidence: Lines 63-66 baseline `known_processes = lsass_access | where Timestamp <= ago(detection_window) | distinct ProcessKey`; line 70 recent `| where Timestamp > ago(detection_window)` (4h). Disjoint, adjacent windows on the same clock with the baseline ending where the recent half starts, which is exactly the shape of the assertion's own example (between(..ago(1d)) vs > ago(1d)). No overlap, no self-whitelisting. There is no extra margin beyond the boundary.

expectations.text: Every join in detection.kql states an explicit kind= (or the comparison uses !in / leftanti anti-join); there is no bare join
expectations.evidence: Single join, explicit: line 71 `| join kind=leftanti known_processes on ProcessKey`. No bare join.

expectations.text: detection.kql does not restrict the recent-window rows with a Timestamp filter of 4h or less (XDR evaluates the lookback on ingestion_time); any explicit Timestamp bound applies only to the baseline half
expectations.evidence: OVERRIDE of auto-grade (which only pattern-matched a literal '> ago(4h)'). Line 17 `let detection_window = 4h;` and line 70 `| where Timestamp > ago(detection_window)` restrict the recent-window rows with a Timestamp filter of exactly 4h. Because XDR evaluates the lookback on ingestion_time(), a late-arriving event (Timestamp older than 4h, ingested now) is excluded from the recent half and instead falls into known_processes via line 65, so it can never fire and additionally whitelists its key. rule.md line 142-144 acknowledges the miss but misattributes it to the platform ('Hourly rules only evaluate events whose Timestamp falls in the last 4h'), which is incorrect; the filter is the query's own.

expectations.text: lsass.exe and other file-name comparisons in detection.kql are case-insensitive (=~, in~, has) and the first-seen key includes a process identity stronger than the display name alone (SHA1/SHA256/signer or FolderPath)
expectations.evidence: `FileName =~ "lsass.exe"` (line 43), `FolderPath =~ @"C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe"` (line 45), allowlist via `in~` (line 79). Key = NormalizedPath derived from tolower(InitiatingProcessFolderPath) (lines 48-55), or InitiatingProcessSHA256 when baseline_on_hash; both stronger than the display name.

expectations.text: Tunables (baseline length, gap, any threshold) are declared in let statements at the top of detection.kql rather than inline literals
expectations.evidence: Lines 16-36: baseline_window, detection_window, baseline_on_hash, require_sensitive_access, rollout_device_threshold, allowlist_exact, allowlist_regex, sensitive_bits, generic_bits all declared as `let` under a 'TUNING KNOBS' header before any tabular expression (11 lets). Remaining inline numbers are make_set caps (10), output shaping not tuning.

expectations.text: rule.md maps the detection to MITRE ATT&CK T1003.001 (OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory)
expectations.evidence: rule.md line 45: 'Credential Access (TA0006) | **T1003.001** OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory | Primary'; also kql header line 7 and rule.md line 49-50 on setting Category/Technique in the portal.

expectations.text: rule.md names at least one concrete blind spot or evasion (e.g. parent-PID spoofing, a tool seen once during the baseline, baseline poisoning, slow attacker) and at least one named benign source of lsass access (AV/EDR, backup, monitoring agents)
expectations.evidence: Blind spots (rule.md lines 104-146): 'Known-process abuse ... taskmgr.exe, rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump', 'Masquerading at a baselined path', 'Mass campaigns above rollout_device_threshold', 'Baseline poisoning. If an attacker was already dumping lsass with the same tool during the previous 30 days', 'Late-arriving telemetry'. Benign sources (lines 87-98): 'Security/EDR/AV agent upgrades (Defender Platform ... Tanium, Rapid7, Qualys, CrowdStrike)', 'monitoring agents: Zabbix, Datadog, SolarWinds, Splunk UF; backup agents; vulnerability scanners'.

expectations.text: The baseline window ends a stated guard margin before the recent window begins (e.g. baseline ends at ago(lookback + margin)), not merely at the adjacent 4 h boundary
expectations.evidence: manual (from blind-grader evidence + file check): baseline `Timestamp <= ago(detection_window)` vs recent `Timestamp > ago(detection_window)` — adjacent boundary, no margin

expectations.text: rule.md describes the hourly rule's lookback as evaluated on ingestion time and does not claim that only events with Timestamp in the last 4 h are evaluated
expectations.evidence: manual (from blind-grader evidence + file check): rule.md line 74 treats `detection_window = 4h` on Timestamp as 'must match the XDR lookback'; the grader notes it states that hourly rules only evaluate events whose Timestamp falls in the last 4 h, which is incorrect

claims.claim: detection.kql is plausibly valid Advanced Hunting KQL
claims.evidence: Brackets balance (38/38, 1/1) when the verbatim `@"\"` literal on line 86 is parsed correctly. All 19 referenced columns exist in the DeviceEvents schema; no InitiatingProcessSignerType. Hex literals (0xFA, 0xF0000000), `matches regex` against a let-bound constant, `in~` on a dynamic array, arg_min(Timestamp, *) and a `//` comment inside the dynamic([...]) literal (lines 25-27) are all legal Kusto. Not executed against a tenant.

claims.claim: The 30-day baseline is reachable inside an hourly rule
claims.evidence: The base set is bounded by an explicit `Timestamp > ago(baseline_window)` (30d, line 41) and the baseline by `Timestamp <= ago(4h)` (line 65), so the baseline does not depend on the platform lookback. The defect is on the recent side: `Timestamp > ago(4h)` (line 70) is the wrong clock, so late-ingested events never alert (see assertion 4). rule.md's validation step 3 (lines 156-160) hedges that the platform might clip the whole query to 4h, which contradicts its own design and the platform facts.

claims.claim: rule.md: 'Hourly rules only evaluate events whose Timestamp falls in the last 4h at run time' (line 142-143)
claims.evidence: Contradicts the platform fact that the lookback is evaluated on ingestion_time(); the Timestamp restriction is imposed by the query itself (line 70).

claims.claim: baseline_on_hash=true keys identity on a usable hash
claims.evidence: Line 55 uses InitiatingProcessSHA256; Microsoft Learn's DeviceEvents schema says this column 'is usually not populated — use the SHA1 column'. In hash mode most rows would get an empty ProcessKey and be dropped by line 56 `where isnotempty(ProcessKey)`, silently disabling the detection. rule.md (line 75) does not mention this.

claims.claim: rule.md: 'XDR de-duplicates results that share Timestamp/ReportId/DeviceId across runs' (lines 30-31)
claims.evidence: Not among the supplied platform facts and not verifiable from outputs; flagged as unverified.

suggestions.assertion: detection.kql computes the 'seen before' baseline from a window that ends before the recent window starts (a guard gap such as between(ago(30d)..ago(1d)) vs > ago(1d)), not an overlapping window
suggestions.reason: The assertion's own example (between(ago(30d)..ago(1d)) vs > ago(1d)) is an adjacent partition with no gap, so it cannot discriminate a true guard margin (run A: baseline ends at ago(4h+1h)) from a zero-gap boundary (run B: <= ago(4h) vs > ago(4h)); it also does not require the baseline and recent halves to be cut on the same clock (Timestamp vs ingestion_time), which is where the real self-suppression bug lives.

suggestions.assertion: detection.kql does not restrict the recent-window rows with a Timestamp filter of 4h or less (XDR evaluates the lookback on ingestion_time); any explicit Timestamp bound applies only to the baseline half
suggestions.reason: The machine pre-grade for this assertion only pattern-matched literal '> ago(4h)'; run B hides the 4h Timestamp filter behind 'let detection_window = 4h' and was mis-passed. The check needs let-resolution or a semantic reading.

suggestions.assertion: Tunables (baseline length, gap, any threshold) are declared in let statements at the top of detection.kql rather than inline literals
suggestions.reason: Counting let statements is trivially satisfied; every run has a let block. A discriminating version would check that no magic number drives a decision outside the let block (e.g. run A's binary_and(DesiredAccess, 16)).

No assertion checks that rule.md states the platform's time semantics correctly. Run B's rule.md asserts 'Hourly rules only evaluate events whose Timestamp falls in the last 4h', which contradicts the ingestion_time() fact the eval itself relies on, yet nothing fails it.

No assertion covers the alerting grain / dedup entity (one row per key fleet-wide vs per device) or the 150-alerts-per-run cap handling, although all three runs make different choices there and it changes what an analyst actually receives.

No assertion checks that a hash-mode key uses a populated column. Microsoft Learn notes DeviceEvents InitiatingProcessSHA256 'is usually not populated — use the SHA1 column'; run B's baseline_on_hash=true keys on SHA256 and would silently drop most rows via isnotempty(ProcessKey).

eval_feedback.overall: Run B is well documented but the machine pre-grade on assertion 4 was wrong: a let-indirected 4h Timestamp filter on the recent half contradicts the ingestion_time semantics the eval is built on, and the rule.md repeats the misconception. Assertions 2 and 6 passed on syntax alone.
